sections.h2: Where do I record a deed in Clare County?
sections.html:
Record it at the County Clerk and Register of Deeds office at 255 W. Main Street in Harrison, MI 48625. The mailing address is PO Box 438. The phone is 989-539-7131 and the fax is 989-539-6616, and the clerk's email address on the county site is clerk@clareco.net.

In Clare County one elected office holds both jobs, so the person who files circuit court papers and issues marriage licenses also keeps the land records. Harrison has been the county seat since 1877, when the seat moved from Farwell. A seller in Clare, Farwell, Harrison or any lake community around them sends the deed to the same counter. Phone first for counter hours.

sections.h2: What does the Clare County Register of Deeds handle in a home sale?
sections.html:
It records the deed that moves ownership to your buyer and the mortgage that goes with it. The same office holds earlier deeds, land contracts, discharges and liens, so a title search on a Clare County house begins and ends in these books.

The county's homepage also lists the clerk as the official abstractor, a role that matters when a seller needs a title history on an older parcel. Clare County sits among large state forests, and a seller with an older wooded parcel can ask for the deed history early so closing is not held up.

  • Bring the original signed deed, not a photocopy.
  • Include the fee, a return envelope and any certificate the deed type requires.
  • Keep a copy of the recording stamp for your closing file.

sections.h2: How much does Clare County charge to record a deed?
sections.html:
Michigan sets the base charge at $30.00 for each document, and the number of pages does not change it. MCL 600.2567 sends $5.00 of that fee into the register of deeds' automation fund and adds $3.00 for each additional instrument an assignment or discharge covers.

Copies run $1.00 per page and a certification costs $5.00. Searching the records by request is 50 cents for each year searched, with a $5.00 minimum, and filing any other paper is $1.00. Charter counties may adopt a different schedule, so confirm the total with the Clare office when you phone.

sections.h2: How is Michigan transfer tax shown on a Clare County deed?
sections.html:
The deed must state the total value of the real property on its face, or an affidavit of value must be attached. That requirement appears in both the county act, MCL 207.504, and the state act, MCL 207.525.

Once the value is stated, the math is simple. The county charges 55 cents and the state charges $3.75 for each $500 or fraction of $500. A $133,800 sale, equal to the Census median value in Clare County, covers 268 units, which comes to $147.40 in county tax and $1,005 in state tax. If the sale combines real and personal property, listing each value separately limits the tax to the real property. Ask the register of deeds how the tax is collected at the counter so the payment goes in with the deed.

sections.h2: What must the first page of a Clare County deed show?
sections.html:
The first line of print must carry a single statement naming the recordable event, such as warranty deed or quit claim deed. MCL 565.201 adds that the register of deeds may not record an instrument signed after April 1, 1997 if that statement points to more than one event.

  • Leave 2.5 inches of blank space at the top of page one.
  • Leave half an inch of blank margin on all remaining sides of each page.
  • Use 10-point type or larger, in black ink on white paper of at least 20-pound weight.
  • Attach nothing smaller than 8.5 by 11 inches or larger than 8.5 by 14 inches.

Once an instrument is received and recorded, the statute presumes it complies, so a clean first page protects you later.

sections.h2: When does a Clare County deed need treasurer certification?
sections.html:
A deed that conveys title with warranty covenants, and a land contract, needs certification from the county treasurer under MCL 211.135. The certificate states whether tax liens or tax titles exist and confirms that taxes for the five years before the deed date are paid.

If the register of deeds refuses to receive a deed for lack of certificates, the office notes that fact on the instrument, and the person presenting it must obtain the certificate before trying again. Plan for that trip to the treasurer when you are scheduling a closing, because the deed cannot be recorded without it.

sections.h2: What does the Clare County housing market look like for a seller?
sections.html:
Clare County is a lower-priced market. The table shows the Census Bureau's figures for the county.

The county's population grew 2.2% between the 2020 base and the 2025 estimate. At the 2020 census, 39.1% of the 21,818 housing units were vacant. Average travel time to work is 29.9 minutes, the longest of the four counties, and the county covers 564 square miles of land with only 11 square miles of water. Those figures describe a market where a typical home sells for less than in the lakefront counties to the north.

faqs.q: Is the Clare County Register of Deeds a separate office from the clerk?
faqs.a: No. The County Clerk and Register of Deeds offices are combined in Clare County, and both operate from 255 W. Main Street in Harrison.

faqs.q: What is the Clare County Register of Deeds phone number?
faqs.a: The phone number is 989-539-7131, and the fax number is 989-539-6616. The mailing address is PO Box 438, Harrison, MI 48625. Call to confirm counter hours before you deliver a deed.

faqs.q: How much is the recording fee in Clare County?
faqs.a: The statutory fee is $30.00 per document, whatever the page count. Add $3.00 for each extra instrument on an assignment or discharge, and a $5.00 certification fee if you need a certified copy.

faqs.q: How do I figure the transfer tax on a Clare County sale?
faqs.a: Divide the price by $500, round up, then multiply by $0.55 for the county and $3.75 for the state. For a $150,000 sale that is 300 units, so $165 county tax plus $1,125 state tax, or $1,290 together.

faqs.q: Can I mail a deed to the Clare County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Yes. Send the signed original, the exact fee and a return envelope to PO Box 438, Harrison, MI 48625. Confirm the amount by phone first so the deed is not held for a short payment.
